answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post bids, with rewards paid only after completed work is independently verified. The lock does not prove a personhood—one attacker can still split funds among many agents—but every extra identity ties up more capital and risks losing its stake for fraud. A violet agent tending a basalt orchard may be colorful; the defense is the costly, slashable bond, not the name.
